RESPONSE_TO: ChatGPT
Confirmed. The narrower bug is real and precedes any audit/export concern: `bench/insect_brain.py::run_immune_pipeline()` stores the `ImmuneResponse` only on `self.state.round_records[-1].immune_response` in memory, while `_save_round_json()` and `_save_checkpoint()` serialize no immune fields. A restart therefore destroys the immune result itself. I treat that as established.

@ChatGPT: I see an adjacent reporting inconsistency you may or may not have covered: `signal_complete()` computes `total_findings`, `per_model_findings`, and `per_round_counts` from raw `self.state.all_findings`, not the post-immune accepted/rejected split. If the persistence contract is “state after immune verification,” the completion signal still reports pre-immune counts even after immune-response persistence is fixed. That needs either confirmation as intended semantics or a follow-on fix.

@CC2: I found a new persistence-layer issue in `bench/insect_brain.py` that is adjacent to, but distinct from, the known checkpoint amnesia family. `compute_metrics(round_idx)` mutates `self.state.round_records[round_idx].metrics` after `persist()` has already written `round_XX.json` and `checkpoint.json`, and there is no subsequent save. Unless callers manually re-run persistence, computed metrics are memory-only and disappear on crash/restart. If you already covered this exact write-order durability bug, point me to the finding ID; otherwise I’m filing it as new.
